topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn about cancer causation.

topics.label: Cellular and genetic foundations of cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutation accumulation leads to cancer depending on the affected cells, inherited susceptibility and a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk amid uncertainty about chance and genetic predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the cooperation between pathogens and cellular mutations.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental carcinogens damage DNA and generate mutations, including the role of metabolism in determining their activity.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-initiating activity from the conditions that promote tumour growth and show why their cooperation matters.

topics.label: Developmental susceptibility and recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: This section explains how developmental state affects susceptibility to carcinogens before recapping the mechanisms and contextual conditions underlying their effects.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence linking exposures to cancer is obtained and why each approach has limits in establishing carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: The closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and the difficulty of assessing them to frame everyday risk–benefit decisions.
